question: A 56-year-old woman presents, after a casual fall to the floor, pain, deformity and increased volume in the left arm, with impossibility for the dorsal flexion of the hand. What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.opa: Trocheter fracture in the left humerus.
options.opb: Diaphyseal fracture of the left humerus with radial nerve injury.
options.opc: Supraconcondylar fracture of the humeral palate with median nerve injury.
options.opd: Fracture of the anatomical neck of the humerus with radial nerve injury.
options.ope: Fracture of displaced epitrochlea with ulnar nerve injury.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Casual fall to the floor -> trauma to the left arm -> pain, deformity, and increased volume in the left arm -> impossibility for dorsal flexion of the hand -> nerve injury likely present -> 70% CHAIN: Casual fall to the floor -> trauma to the left arm -> pain, deformity, and increased volume in the left arm -> impossibility for dorsal flexion of the hand -> radial nerve involvement suspected -> 80% CHAIN: Casual fall to the floor -> trauma to the left arm -> pain, deformity, and increased volume in the left arm -> impossibility for dorsal flexion of the hand -> radial nerve injury commonly associated with humeral fractures -> 90% CHAIN: Casual fall to the floor -> trauma to the left arm -> pain, deformity, and increased volume in the left arm -> impossibility for dorsal flexion of the hand -> likely radial nerve injury -> Diaphyseal fracture of the left humerus with radial nerve injury is the most likely diagnosis -> 70%
analysis: Based on the presentation of pain, deformity, and inability for dorsal flexion of the hand following a fall, along with the specific nerve involvement, the most likely diagnosis is a diaphyseal fracture of the left humerus with radial nerve injury.
